key_insight: The paper introduces Step-Decomposed Influence (SDI), which breaks a single scalar TracIn score into a length-τ sequence that reveals when (which recurrent iteration) a training example affects a looped transformer’s computation. This exposes the temporal footprint of training-data influence during latent iterative reasoning.
problem_solved: Existing influence estimators collapse influence across all recurrent iterations, hiding when during the looped (τ-step) computation a training example is important.
method: Decompose TracIn into per-step contributions by computing influence at each of the τ recurrent iterations of the shared transformer block.
Produce an influence trace (length-τ vector) for each training example showing its step-resolved effect on model states or loss.
Use these traces for attribution analyses, debugging, and targeted dataset/model interventions (e.g., censoring or editing examples that matter at specific steps).
impact: SDI gives practitioners temporal resolution on data influence in looped transformers, enabling precise debugging, targeted data curation, and more interpretable reasoning-chain analyses without changing the training setup.
visual_elements: Timeline/line plot: influence magnitude vs. iteration step (length-τ) for selected training examples to show when each example matters.
Heatmap: examples (rows) × steps (columns) colored by influence to reveal patterns (early vs. late influence, clustered behaviors).
Schematic diagram: looped transformer with a shared block repeated τ times and arrows mapping a training example to per-step influence signals.
Bar chart comparison: aggregated TracIn scalar vs. SDI summary (e.g., max-step or step-of-peak) to illustrate information lost by aggregation.
paper_title: Step-resolved data attribution for looped transformers
paper_authors: Georgios Kaissis, David Mildenberger, Juan Felipe Gomez, Martin J. Menten, Eleni Triantafillou
